# Geovisualisation {#sec-m2-mapas}

Two kinds of map, with different purposes: the **static** map, which goes into the report, and the
**interactive** map, which is for checking the data and for publishing online. This chapter covers the
essentials of both; publication finishing is the subject of module 5.

```{r}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

arquivo <- "dados/brutos/muni_pr_sc.gpkg"
if (!file.exists(arquivo)) {
  muni <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    geobr::read_municipality(code_muni = "PR", year = 2022, showProgress = FALSE),
    geobr::read_municipality(code_muni = "SC", year = 2022, showProgress = FALSE)
  )
  sf::st_write(muni, arquivo, quiet = TRUE)
}
muni <- sf::st_read(arquivo, quiet = TRUE)

portos <- data.frame(
  nome = c("Paranaguá", "Antonina", "São Francisco do Sul", "Itajaí", "Imbituba"),
  tku_bi = c(21.4, 1.2, 8.7, 6.3, 3.1),
  lon = c(-48.5119, -48.7119, -48.6383, -48.6486, -48.6706),
  lat = c(-25.5016, -25.4283, -26.2400, -26.9077, -28.2300)
) |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
```

## `geom_sf`: the map in `ggplot2`

`geom_sf()` draws any `sf` object and works out on its own whether it is a point, line or polygon.
All of module 1's grammar still applies.

```{r}
#| label: fig-mapa-base
#| fig-cap: "Minimal map"
#| fig-height: 4
ggplot(muni) + geom_sf()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-mapa-coropletico
#| fig-cap: "Choropleth: area of the municipalities"
#| fig-height: 4.6
muni |>
  dplyr::mutate(area_km2 = as.numeric(units::set_units(sf::st_area(geom), km^2))) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = area_km2), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, transform = "log10",
                       name = "Area (km²)",
                       labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ",")) +
  theme_void(base_size = 10)
```

The choropleth rule: **colour in a polygon represents a rate or density, not a total**. Mapping
absolute population by municipality colours the map by the size of the municipality, not by the phenomenon.
For totals, use proportional symbols.

## Layers, proportional symbols and labels

```{r}
#| label: fig-mapa-camadas
#| fig-cap: "Municipalities, ports with symbols proportional to TKU, and labels"
#| fig-height: 5.4
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = muni, fill = "grey96", colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = portos, aes(size = tku_bi), colour = "#1a5b8a", alpha = 0.75) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = portos,
    aes(label = nome, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates", size = 2.8, min.segment.length = 0
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 10), name = "TKU (billion t·km)") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-49.5, -47.8), ylim = c(-28.8, -25.0)) +
  labs(caption = "Illustrative values.") +
  theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

Three technical details in this block:

- `stat = "sf_coordinates"` with `aes(geometry = ...)` is what lets `ggrepel` push apart
  overlapping labels on a map.
- `coord_sf(xlim, ylim)` crops the **view**, without changing the data.
- The order of the layers is the drawing order: base first, points last.

## Scale bar, north arrow and coordinate grid

```{r}
#| label: fig-mapa-ggspatial
#| fig-cap: "Cartographic elements with ggspatial"
#| fig-height: 5
litoral <- muni |>
  dplyr::filter(name_muni %in% c("Paranaguá", "Antonina", "Morretes", "Guaratuba",
                          "Matinhos", "Pontal do Paraná", "Guaraqueçaba"))

ggplot(litoral) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = name_muni), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = portos |> dplyr::filter(nome %in% c("Paranaguá", "Antonina")),
          colour = "black", size = 2) +
  ggspatial::annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.25) +
  ggspatial::annotation_north_arrow(
    location = "tr", style = ggspatial::north_arrow_minimal(),
    height = unit(1, "cm"), width = unit(1, "cm")
  ) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues", name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "The coast of Paraná",
       caption = "Source: IBGE, 2022 municipal boundaries (geobr).") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.2))
```

A map that goes into an official document needs: a title, a source, a scale bar, a north
indicator and a mention of the coordinate system. The first two go in `labs()`; the next two
in `ggspatial`; the last one in the legend or in the document's footnote.

## Panels

```{r}
#| label: fig-mapa-facet
#| fig-cap: "One panel per state, with independent spatial scale"
#| fig-height: 3.6
muni |>
  dplyr::mutate(area_km2 = as.numeric(units::set_units(sf::st_area(geom), km^2))) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = area_km2), colour = NA) +
  facet_wrap(~abbrev_state) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, transform = "log10", name = "km²") +
  theme_void(base_size = 9)
```

## Interactive maps

### `leaflet`: interactive maps for publication

```{r}
leaflet::leaflet(portos) |>
  leaflet::addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") |>
  leaflet::addCircleMarkers(
    radius = ~sqrt(tku_bi) * 2,
    color = "#1a5b8a", fillOpacity = 0.6, stroke = FALSE,
    popup = ~paste0("<b>", nome, "</b><br>TKU: ", tku_bi, " billion t·km")
  ) |>
  leaflet::addPolygons(data = sf::st_transform(litoral, 4326),
              fillColor = "#e07b39", fillOpacity = 0.2,
              color = "white", weight = 1, label = ~name_muni) |>
  leaflet::addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft")
```

`leaflet` requires **geographic coordinates** (`EPSG:4326`): if the data are in UTM, it
complains or draws wrongly. `sf::st_transform(x, 4326)` before plotting solves it.

::: {.callout-note}
## Basemap without an access key

Some basemap providers now require an API key: `CartoDB.Positron`, widely
used in tutorials, now appears covered by "API KEY REQUIRED". For a light, neutral
background without registration, use `Esri.WorldGrayCanvas`; for satellite, `Esri.WorldImagery`; for the
street map, `OpenStreetMap`. The full list is in `names(leaflet::providers)`.
:::

### `mapview`: quick visual checks

::: {.callout-tip}
## The most valuable use of an interactive map is not publishing. It is checking

Before trusting any spatial result, throw the layer into a `mapview` over a satellite
image and look: does the *buffer* cover what it should? Did the points land on the road or in the bush?
Did the clip get the right municipality? Five seconds of visual checking avoid a wrong
report. Unlike `leaflet`, `mapview` does not require reprojecting to `EPSG:4326` or building
layer by layer. It is one line, with a basemap selector (satellite included) ready to use.
:::

For example, to check the Paraná coast subset made above:

```{r}
area_analise <- litoral

mapview::mapview(area_analise, map.types = "Esri.WorldImagery")
```

Note that `litoral` is in SIRGAS 2000 (`EPSG:4674`), and `mapview` reprojected it on its own.

### `mapgl`: modern vector maps

`mapgl` exposes MapLibre/Mapbox GL, with vector rendering, 3D extrusion and smooth
transitions. It is the best option when the interactive map is the final product: a dashboard for the
Undersecretariat, for example.

```{r}
library(mapgl)

mapgl::maplibre(bounds = portos, height = "525px") |>   # without height, the map takes 750 px
  mapgl::add_circle_layer(
    id = "portos",
    source = portos,
    circle_color = "#1a5b8a",
    circle_radius = 8,
    circle_opacity = 0.7,
    tooltip = "nome"
  )
```

In module 5 we come back to interactive maps inside Quarto reports, where they sit alongside
text and tables.

## Saving maps

```{r}
#| eval: false
mapa <- ggplot(litoral) + geom_sf()

ggsave("resultados/mapa_litoral.png", mapa,
       width = 18, height = 14, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
ggsave("resultados/mapa_litoral.pdf", mapa,
       width = 18, height = 14, units = "cm")        # vector, for printing
```

For maps, prefer PDF or SVG: lines and labels stay sharp at any magnification, which
matters when the document is printed on A3 or projected.
